items.title: La Vaca Coworking

content.text: La Vaca is a big former dairy turned into a creative and relaxed Coworking in Barcelona city center, district of Poble Sec. Once, people used to get milk from this space; and now we are working from a vibrant and dynamic space called “La Vaca” which meand “The Cow”. We have a self service Cafeteria where we provide water, tea, coffee and milk for free. A bright and spacious ground floor where there are plenty of comfortable workstations. In the Basement we have a meeting room and other shared desks. Skype room, projectors, printer and scanner are also provided. Chill in our comfortable living room and just feel at home at la Vaca.
What really makes La Vaca Coworking special is our vibrant and strong community, genuine connections and friendships among our coworkers.

content.text: Discover the charm of Amsterdam at The Bee Hostel, your home away from home since our grand opening in July 2022. Nestled near the enchanting Artis Zoo in the city center, our hostel offers a unique and welcoming experience for travelers seeking both comfort and style.

What sets The Bee Hostel apart is our commitment to providing a comfortable stay with hospitality and a personalized experience. Step into our exclusive Ladies-Only dorm or our Unisex Dormitories with uniquely designed beds with the look of the bee hives, all beds come equipped with a privacy curtain and an electrical panel with a reading light and charger. We are offering privacy and practical space in the heart of the vibrant city.

Experience luxury on a budget at The Bee Hostel, where our facilities seamlessly blend comfort, style, and cleanliness. Our beds are not just a place to rest; they are a statement, reflecting our dedication to providing a memorable stay. Whether you're a solo traveler, a group of friends, or a globetrotting adventurer, The Bee Hostel has a space for all, ensuring a stay that is both affordable and unique.

Indulge in the pleasure of a cozy, and thoughtfully designed facility that makes The Bee Hostel the perfect base for your Amsterdam exploration. Discover a new standard of hospitality at The Bee Hostel, where every stay is an invitation to enjoy the best of Amsterdam in comfort and style.
It's an experience—a place where luxury meets budget without compromising on quality.

items.title: The Nomad Escape

content.text: The Nomad Escape is a business and networking club tailored for location-independent professionals, entrepreneurs, and remote teams. It specializes in organizing transformative retreats and events in exotic locations, focusing on expanding networks, enhancing skills, and fostering a growth mindset.

: Originally from the Netherlands, Michelle is the Founder and CEO of The Nomad Escape. Her journey into the digital nomad lifestyle began around 2019 when she started traveling as a solo backpacker in Australia. With a passion for connecting like-minded individuals, she has developed exclusive programs for location-independent entrepreneurs and remote professionals, creating a diverse and supportive community.

The Nomad Escape aims to provide a friendly and informal environment where professionals can connect without the formalities of traditional networking. Their retreats and events are designed to help individuals unplug from work, focus on personal and professional growth, and build meaningful relationships.
: Offering a range of experiences, including business retreats like the Level Up Club and larger gatherings such as the Nomad Island Fest, held in locations like Madeira, Portugal.
: An invite-only virtual network club for location-independent entrepreneurs, facilitating bespoke introductions to help grow their businesses.
: Emphasizing a no-pitching, no-business-cards approach, encouraging participants to come as they are and connect authentically with others.

The Nomad Escape continues to expand its offerings, with upcoming events such as the Level Up Club Business Retreat in March 2025 and the Nomad Island Fest in December 2025, both scheduled to take place in Madeira, Portugal.
For a more in-depth understanding of Michelle Maree’s journey and the mission of The Nomad Escape, you might find the following interview informative:
World travels with the Founder & CEO of The Nomad Escape

items.title: Nomad Cruise

content.text: Nomad Cruise is a pioneering initiative that combines travel with professional development, offering digital nomads, entrepreneurs, and remote workers a unique opportunity to connect and learn while sailing to various destinations. Founded in 2015 by Johannes Voelkner, it has become a significant event in the digital nomad community.

: Originally from Germany, Johannes has been a digital nomad for over a decade. He founded Nomad Cruise to address the need for community and connection among remote workers. Under his leadership, Nomad Cruise has organized multiple voyages, bringing together like-minded individuals to share experiences and knowledge.

Nomad Cruise aims to create a collaborative environment where digital nomads and entrepreneurs can network, learn, and grow. The cruises feature workshops, talks, and networking events tailored to the needs of location-independent professionals.
: Each cruise includes a comprehensive program of workshops and talks covering topics relevant to digital nomads and entrepreneurs.
: Participants have the chance to connect with a diverse group of professionals from around the world, fostering collaborations and friendships.
: The cruises visit various destinations, allowing participants to explore new places while engaging in professional development.

After a hiatus due to global events, Nomad Cruise has resumed its voyages. Recent trips have included destinations such as Antarctica and routes from Canada to Japan, offering participants unique experiences and opportunities to connect.
For a more in-depth understanding of Nomad Cruise and its impact on the digital nomad community, you might find the following interview informative:
Finding Connection as a Nomad with Nomad Cruise Founder Johannes Voelkner

items.title: Running Remote

content.text: Running Remote is a leading conference and community dedicated to providing actionable strategies and insights for building and scaling remote and hybrid teams. Founded by Rob Rawson and Liam Martin, the initiative has been instrumental in shaping the discourse around distributed workforces and remote team management.

: Co-founder and CEO of Time Doctor, an eight-figure SaaS business with over 130 full-time team members across 31 countries, all working remotely. Rob is also the co-author of “Running Remote: Master the Lessons from the World’s Most Successful Remote-Work Pioneers,” a comprehensive guide on remote and asynchronous work.

: Co-founder of Time Doctor and co-author of the “Running Remote” book alongside Rob Rawson. Liam has been a prominent advocate for remote work, sharing insights and strategies through various platforms to help organizations transition to and excel in remote work environments.

Running Remote aims to equip remote-first founders and hybrid-team leaders with the knowledge, connections, and solutions necessary to build and lead remote teams to excellence. The conference covers every facet of building a remote team, addressing challenges such as establishing a strong remote culture, collaborating across time zones, and transitioning from office-based to remote-first companies.
: Running Remote offers high-energy conference days featuring keynotes from successful founders, interactive panels, and hands-on workshops designed to inspire and educate attendees.
: The platform fosters a collaborative environment where participants can share experiences, learn from each other, and build lasting relationships.
: With events held in various international locations, Running Remote attracts a diverse group of attendees, reflecting the global nature of the remote work movement.

Running Remote continues to host events that address the evolving challenges of remote and hybrid work environments. The upcoming conference in Lisbon, scheduled for April 22-24, 2024, will feature over 50 industry experts and 40+ sessions, focusing on the latest strategies in flexible work, company culture, scaling, transitioning, AI, and more.
For more insights into the principles and strategies advocated by Running Remote, you might find the following resource informative:
Running Remote - Liam Martin + Rob Rawson

NomadMania

content.text: NomadMania is a comprehensive platform that categorizes the world into 1,301 regions, encouraging travelers to explore beyond traditional boundaries. Founded by Harry Mitsidis, a seasoned traveler who has visited every country twice, NomadMania offers tools for travelers to track their journeys, discover new destinations, and connect with a global community.

: Born in London to a Greek father and South African mother, Harry’s multicultural background fueled his passion for travel. By the age of 36, he had visited every UN-recognized country and has since completed this feat twice. In 2012, he founded NomadMania (initially known as The Best Travelled) to provide a structured platform for travelers to document and expand their explorations.

NomadMania’s mission is to connect independent travelers, inspiring them to engage in deep, meaningful, and sustainable exploration. The platform values diversity, inclusivity, and integrity, viewing travel as a transformative experience that broadens horizons and fosters global understanding.
: The platform divides the world into 1,301 regions, encouraging travelers to explore beyond standard country lists.
: NomadMania verifies the travel claims of its members, ensuring authenticity within its community.
: The platform fosters a community of serious travelers, promoting education and awareness around travel to make the world more accessible and rewarding for all.

Under Harry’s leadership, NomadMania has expanded its reach, introducing new lists like “Many Quirky Places” to challenge travelers further. The platform also emphasizes ethical travel, encouraging respect and empathy for all destinations.

items.title: Digital Nomad Soul

content.text: Resources and advice for digital nomads including remote job sites.
Aims to help individuals make a remote income to create a digital nomad lifestyle, providing resources and guidance for aspiring nomads.

Denise Mai is a travel enthusiast and remote work advocate who has been exploring the world since 2008, visiting and living in over 80 countries. In her mid-twenties, she decided to leave the corporate world, seeking freedom and flexibility through a location-independent lifestyle. She began her journey by taking on online content writing jobs, which eventually led to a full-time remote career. Over the years, Denise has worked as a remote employee, freelancer, and built her own six-figure online business. Her mission is to share her experiences and knowledge to help others achieve a remote career and embrace the digital nomad lifestyle.
Digital Nomad Soul offers a variety of content aimed at assisting individuals in transitioning to and thriving within a location-independent lifestyle. Key topics include:
: Tips on finding remote jobs, enhancing productivity, and maintaining a healthy work-life balance.
: Insights into becoming a digital nomad, including essential questions to consider and common mistakes to avoid.
: Lessons learned from over 15 years of traveling, focusing on personal growth and adaptability.
: Information on budgeting, minimalistic living, and selecting suitable destinations for digital nomads.
Denise’s firsthand experiences and practical advice make Digital Nomad Soul a valuable resource for anyone interested in remote work and the digital nomad lifestyle.
Denise Mai, the founder of Digital Nomad Soul, maintains an active online presence through various platforms. Here are the social media links associated with her and Digital Nomad Soul:
: Denise shares insights and experiences related to the digital nomad lifestyle on her TikTok account.
: The Digital Nomad Soul Facebook page offers resources and community engagement for remote workers and digital nomads.
: Denise publishes articles on Medium, providing in-depth information on remote work and location-independent living.

items.title: Freaking Nomads

content.text: Freaking Nomads is an online publication and community dedicated to digital nomads—individuals who live and work remotely from various locations worldwide. The platform offers guides, tips, inspiration, and resources to support people in embracing and thriving in the digital nomad lifestyle.

in 2022. Irene, a UX/UI and Product Designer with experience in London startups, felt a lack of belonging due to her Italian-Chinese heritage. This personal journey inspired her to create a space where individuals seeking their own paths could find support and community.

Luca, formerly a marketer in London, transitioned to a digital nomad lifestyle after experiencing panic attacks during the COVID-19 pandemic, which led him to reevaluate his priorities. He became a freelance SEO consultant, allowing him to work and travel simultaneously. Together with Irene, he co-founded Freaking Nomads to inspire others to pursue unconventional paths and find happiness wherever they go.

Freaking Nomads aims to challenge misconceptions about digital nomadism and provide authentic, unfiltered insights into the lifestyle. The platform emphasizes inclusivity and diversity, striving to create a safe environment for all digital nomads to feel themselves and connect with like-minded individuals.
The platform has been featured in various publications, including Condé Nast Traveller Middle East, Travel + Leisure, and Forbes, highlighting its impact and relevance in the digital nomad community.

content.text: Nomad Summit originally was created by Johnny FD in Chiang Mai. He stopped because of Covid.

in Summer 2024 he sold it to Christoph and Kai, but not related to his insurance business. Both of them have strong relationships with Estonia E-residency and I think the do this event for a Estonia residency purposes.
Curves.Digital was recommended to Christoph some time ago, and they did the whole rebranding for them.

Nomad Summit is a premier conference series that brings together digital nomads, remote workers, and entrepreneurs to share knowledge, network, and collaborate. Founded in 2015 by Johnny FD, the summit has hosted events in various locations, including Chiang Mai, Thailand, which is renowned as a hub for digital nomads.

: Born Johnny Jen, he is a location-independent entrepreneur who left his corporate job in 2008 to pursue a life of travel and online business. Johnny has been instrumental in building communities for digital nomads and has been featured in various publications for his work.
Christoph and Kai. They bought it in summer 2024.

Nomad Summit aims to unite and empower individuals passionate about building businesses, skills, and communities. The conference serves as an open platform where tech enthusiasts, indie hackers, and creators come together to create meaningful ventures and connections.
: The summit offers high-energy conference days featuring keynotes from successful founders, interactive panels, and hands-on workshops designed to inspire and educate attendees.
: Nomad Summit fosters a collaborative environment where participants can share experiences, learn from each other, and build lasting relationships.
: With events held in various international locations, Nomad Summit attracts a diverse group of attendees, reflecting the global nature of the digital nomad movement.

After a hiatus, Nomad Summit is set to return to Chiang Mai in January 2025, reviving its mission to support and inspire the digital nomad community. The upcoming event will feature a dynamic weekend conference packed with engaging sessions and a week of side events organized by the community

items.title: Nomad Flag

content.text: A monthly curated collection of stories, hacks, advice, and tools for digital nomads, travelers, and location-independent entrepreneurs.

Nomad Flag is a travel and lifestyle blog dedicated to independent travelers, digital nomads, expats, and culture enthusiasts. The platform offers a wealth of information, including travel advice, destination guides, and insights into the digital nomad lifestyle.

Nomad Flag was founded by Keith, an Irish traveler and blogger with over two decades of experience living overseas. His extensive travels have taken him to various parts of the world, and he shares his experiences and knowledge through the blog.
The blog covers a wide range of topics, including:
: Tips and tricks to make travel more efficient and affordable.
: Insights into expatriate life, including cultural experiences and practical advice.
: Explorations of global cuisines and dining experiences.
: Guides and stories aimed at solo travelers seeking adventure and personal growth.
: Resources for those interested in or currently living a location-independent lifestyle.
Nomad Flag maintains an active online presence, including a Facebook page where followers can find additional content and updates.

content.text: Curated by Chris Cerra, this bi-monthly newsletter focuses on budget-friendly Airbnb deals across Europe, Asia, and Latin America, catering to digital nomads seeking affordable accommodations.

RemoteBase is a platform dedicated to assisting digital nomads in finding affordable accommodations worldwide. Founded by Chris Cerra, it offers a bi-monthly newsletter featuring budget-friendly Airbnb deals across Europe, Asia, and Latin America, catering to digital nomads seeking cost-effective living options.

Chris Cerra is a digital nomad and accommodation expert who began his journey in 2018, traveling while working and spending 1–3 months in various locations. Recognizing the challenges digital nomads face in finding affordable and suitable accommodations, he founded RemoteBase to share curated deals and insights with the nomad community.
: The newsletter provides subscribers with handpicked Airbnb deals that are budget-friendly and located in popular digital nomad destinations.
: Subscribers receive updates every two weeks, ensuring they have access to the latest accommodation options.
: The service primarily focuses on Europe, Asia, and Latin America, regions known for their vibrant digital nomad communities.
RemoteBase aims to simplify the accommodation search process for digital nomads, enabling them to focus more on their work and travel experiences.
For more information or to subscribe to the newsletter, visit RemoteBase’s official website:

items.title: Nomadic Matt's

content.text: Offers practical advice on traveling better, cheaper, and longer, featuring stories from travelers, destination guides, travel deals, and exclusive content.

Nomadic Matt is a leading travel website founded by Matthew Kepnes, dedicated to helping individuals travel better, cheaper, and longer. The platform offers comprehensive guides, tips, and resources for travelers seeking to explore the world on a budget.

Matthew Kepnes, known online as Nomadic Matt, is an American travel writer and blogger from Boston, Massachusetts. He earned a Bachelor’s Degree in Education from the University of Massachusetts Amherst in 2003 and later completed a Master of Business Administration at Suffolk University. In 2005, after a transformative trip to Thailand, he decided to quit his job and embark on a journey to travel the world. This experience inspired him to start blogging about his adventures, leading to the creation of Nomadic Matt in 2008.
Matthew is the author of several travel-related books, including:
How to Travel the World on $50 a Day: Travel Cheaper, Longer, Smarter
Ten Years a Nomad: A Traveler’s Journey Home
His first book became a New York Times bestseller, offering practical advice for budget travelers.

Under Matthew’s guidance, Nomadic Matt has grown to become one of the most visited travel blogs globally, attracting over a million visitors per month. The website provides a wealth of information, including destination guides, travel tips, and resources to help travelers plan and execute their trips efficiently.

Matthew’s mission is to demystify the art of budget travel and make it accessible to everyone. Through his website, books, and courses, he aims to inspire and equip individuals to explore the world without breaking the bank

items.title: The Remote Nomad

content.text: Provides insights and tips on finding remote work, traveling the world, and living a fulfilling life, along with interviews and resources for digital nomads.

The Remote Nomad® is a platform founded by Kate Smith, dedicated to helping professionals transition from traditional office roles to remote careers. Since June 2015, Kate has been working remotely while traveling to over 25 countries. She left her corporate 9-5 job in advertising to pursue a full-time remote position in online marketing before launching her own business. Her mission is to assist others in achieving the freedom and flexibility that remote work offers.
Services Offered by The Remote Nomad®
: Personalized guidance to help individuals land remote jobs.
: A comprehensive program designed to provide step-by-step strategies for securing remote employment.
: A resource offering insights and tips for aspiring remote workers.
: Regular content discussing remote work, job search strategies, and the digital nomad lifestyle.

Kate’s expertise has been featured in major publications such as BBC, Fast Company, CNN, Atlas Obscura, and GlassDoor. She was named among the Top 100 Most Influential Remote Work Experts in RemoteWeekly. Additionally, she collaborated with the country of Estonia to create the world’s first digital nomad visa.

items.title: Nomad Soulmates

content.text: Nomad Soulmates is a platform designed to connect single digital nomads, remote workers, and location-independent professionals seeking meaningful relationships and friendships. Founded by Aline Dahmen and Sebastien Pelletier, the platform addresses the unique challenges of dating and building connections while leading a nomadic lifestyle.

: Originally from Germany, Aline became a digital nomad and community leader, co-founding Nomad Soulmates to help others find meaningful connections while traveling. She has been instrumental in building and nurturing the community, which began as a Facebook group and later expanded into a dedicated app.

: Co-founder of Nomad Soulmates, Sebastien collaborated with Aline to create a platform that facilitates connections among digital nomads, addressing the common issue of loneliness in the nomadic community.

Nomad Soulmates started as a Facebook group, fostering a community where like-minded individuals could connect and share experiences. Recognizing the need for a more tailored solution, the founders developed a dedicated dating app designed specifically for digital nomads and remote workers. The app aims to provide a user-friendly experience, enabling users to find partners who understand and share the nomadic lifestyle.

The platform has grown significantly, with the Facebook group amassing over 17,000 members. Nomad Soulmates emphasizes creating a respectful and supportive environment, helping members build deep, meaningful connections, whether romantic or platonic.

items.title: Nomad Cloud

content.text: A weekly 5-minute newsletter delivering key insights into travel, remote work, and the digital nomad lifestyle, read by over 250,000 subscribers.

Nomad Cloud is a leading newsletter dedicated to the digital nomad lifestyle, offering subscribers weekly insights into travel, remote work, and location-independent living. With over 300,000 subscribers, it provides a concise 5-minute read each week, covering topics that help individuals navigate and thrive in a nomadic work environment.
The platform is spearheaded by a team of experienced digital nomads and entrepreneurs:
: An expert in email marketing and entrepreneurship, Adam has successfully built a career while traveling to some of the world’s most captivating destinations.
: With a background in digital marketing, Gabi combines professional endeavors with a passion for global exploration, embodying the work-from-anywhere ethos.
: A leader in remote work advocacy, Pranam focuses on expanding the intersection of work and adventure, helping others achieve financial success and personal fulfillment through a nomadic lifestyle.

Since 2019, their collective adventures have taken them across Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and the Pacific Isles. Their mission is to assist one million travelers in breaking free from conventional routines to achieve both financial prosperity and global exploration. Their work has been featured in major publications like CNBC, Forbes, Inc., and Business Insider, highlighting their contributions to marketing and entrepreneurship.

Nomad Cloud offers a free subscription to its weekly newsletter, providing readers with key insights into the digital nomad lifestyle. Subscribers receive curated content that includes travel tips, remote work opportunities, and lifestyle hacks tailored for location-independent professionals.

items.title: A Brother Abroad

content.text: Offers insights into becoming a successful digital nomad, sharing experiences and advice from extensive travels across numerous countries.

A Brother Abroad is a travel blog and resource hub founded by Carlos Grider, a former U.S. Marine and MBA-level marketer. The platform offers insights into travel, digital nomadism, fitness, and personal development, aiming to inspire and equip individuals to embark on their own adventures.

Carlos’s journey began in a small Californian desert town, where he developed a curiosity about the world beyond his immediate surroundings. Seeking exposure and education, he enlisted in the United States Marine Corps, which provided him with opportunities to experience diverse cultures and environments. His military service, including deployments to the Middle East, deepened his appreciation for global exposure and travel.

After his military career, Carlos pursued an MBA specializing in marketing and entered the corporate world as a management consultant. However, he found this path unfulfilling and decided to realign his life with his passions for travel, exploration, and storytelling. This led to the creation of A Brother Abroad, where he shares his experiences and guides others in pursuing unconventional lifestyles.
A Brother Abroad covers a wide range of topics, including:
: Detailed information on destinations, itineraries, and cultural insights.
: Advice on remote work, location independence, and sustaining a nomadic lifestyle.
: Guides on maintaining physical health while traveling, including workouts and nutrition tips.
: Strategies for financial independence, budgeting, and investing as a traveler.
Carlos’s mission is to motivate others to explore the world, challenge their perceptions, and live fulfilling lives aligned with their passions.

items.title: MileMethod

content.text: MileMethod is a personalized service founded by Trevor Wright in 2014, designed to help clients earn and redeem U.S. credit card signup bonuses to travel worldwide at minimal costs. Trevor’s journey into the world of travel hacking began in 2011 when he applied for his first credit card and redeemed its signup bonus for a $71 round-trip flight to Japan. This experience led him to develop a system that has enabled him to average $18 per flight to over 139 countries and book luxury hotel stays worth $183,868 for just $1,612.

Through MileMethod, Trevor offers a one-on-one service that guides clients in applying for specific credit cards, unlocking bonuses through everyday spending, and redeeming those bonuses for luxury travel experiences. The service boasts an average trip discount of 92%, with clients earning over 1.2 million points in 18 months and booking vacations valued at $20,000.

Trevor’s expertise has been featured in various interviews and podcasts, where he shares insights on maximizing credit card rewards for travel. Notably, he appeared on the Expat Money Show, discussing strategies to travel the world for (almost) free

Agreement:

To start small, I’d love to invite one of the founders to share the story behind GetCroissant in our fourth edition—either as a founder-written piece or a co-created interview. We can define the best angle together.

I’d also love to invite you to add GetCroissant to our Nomad Directory, which lives online. It only takes a few quick questions to submit information you want to be published. 

We’re also open to joining the GetCroissant affiliate program.

• Explore a backlink swap between our websites—this could be through partner logos on our homepage or guest articles.

• Social media collab / cross-posts—we can share your news, stats, or new coworking spaces joining the program.

Croissant is a flexible coworking platform founded in 2015 in New York City. It offers members access to a network of over 400 coworking spaces across cities like New York, San Francisco, and London, providing a flexible workspace solution for professionals. 

The company was established by a group of friends who initially collaborated in coffee shops and valued the freedom of working in diverse environments. This experience inspired them to create Croissant, aiming to provide a more structured yet flexible workspace alternative. 

The founding team includes:

• David Idell: Co-founder and current Chief Executive Officer.

• Nisha Garigarn: Co-founder. 

• Zoltan Szalas and Adam Chew: Co-founders. 

Croissant has participated in notable startup programs, including the 500 Startups accelerator, which provided seed funding and mentorship to support its growth.

The platform continues to expand, offering professionals the flexibility to work from various inspiring locations worldwide, fostering productivity and community among its users.

⚙️ Priorities & Approach

• Simplicity and sustainability: They aren’t aggressively marketing or chasing growth; instead, they prioritize organic development and maintaining the quality of their product.

• Word of mouth remains their most powerful growth tool.

• They onboard ambassadors who help with occasional shoutouts.

• They’re open to affiliate partnerships, offering either:

• A unique landing page for a private community discount (30% off for 3 months), or

• An affiliate link that pays $20 or €15 per signup.

🧩 Challenges

• No major “pain points” were explicitly mentioned, but a few implied struggles include:

• Limited internal bandwidth to explore and manage collaborations (Jordan himself is not the final decision-maker)

• Not being focused on traditional marketing tactics or active outreach

• Selective presence: Their reach is stronger in European cities (e.g., Lisbon, Barcelona, Berlin) and weaker in Southeast Asia, which limits engagement in certain nomad hotspots.

✅ How They’ve Made It Work

• Excellent product & service: Their reputation and quality drive long-term user retention and referrals.

• Strong partner onboarding: They continuously add coworking spaces based on demand and availability.

• Nurturing over hustling: They maintain and nurture relationships rather than pushing aggressive sales or marketing.

• Community-first mindset: Personal connections and a close-knit nomad ecosystem play a central role in their continued growth.

items.title: Workspace 6

content.text: Workspace 6 was founded in 2010 and has been a hub for the creative scene in Amsterdam ever since. Visitors are alway initialy greeted by a mural by local graffiti legends, The London Police and walls, ceilings and aisles of bikes. Our community spans the gamut from graphic & industrial design to cacoa & kombucha entrepreneurs and, of course, web developers, marketeers, Blockchain, bike PR and even the occasional local cafe owner who we source our coffee beans from.

We have a jazz series with local label Dox Records, screen films, host rides, and serves as a messenger alleycat checkpoint several times a year. We’re mobbed by BMX’ers every summer for the Bounty Hunters Jam and always have our ramps ready to roll out for impromptu sessions on the bike or skateboard.

One of our confernce rooms is also a music studio with guitar, bass & PA + drums, piano and even a flat screen with an Nintendo 64 and old Xbox! We love to lunch together either in our dining room, on our patio or around the corner on the water. We’re frequently visited by friends, friends of friends and new firends that are freelancers looking for the coziest, most welcoming spot to hang, work, ride & shred situated under the tracks of Central Station!

Pet-Friendly: It's one of the few places that welcome pets, making it a much more inclusive and enjoyable environment for animal lovers. (By Joel Gonçalves)

Excellent Amenities and Flexibility: With 24/7 access, modern facilities, and a variety of workspace solutions (from single desks to warehouses), it adapts to every need. (By Joel Gonçalves)

Great Location: It's well-located near the river, offering the perfect opportunity for a refreshing stroll along the water during a break. (By Joel Gonçalves)

Great Accessibility: Easy to get to via public transport and bike paths, with the bonus of free parking nearby. (By Joel Gonçalves)

content.text: I hope this message finds you well! I’m not entirely sure if this is the right place to pitch a travel story idea, but I wanted to reach out and share a concept I believe could resonate with your readers.
What does it look like to travel for healing when you’re not broke, but still budgeting? When you’re not a perfectly curated influencer, but you’re not exactly off the grid either?

I’m currently living in Thailand and will be spending three weeks in Cambodia next month on a visa run. I’ll be spending ten days immersed in the spiritual gravity of Angkor Wat, and ten days unwinding on the calm shores of Sokha Beach, on a journey that lives in the in-between: between burnout and breakthrough, indulgence and intention, tourist and storyteller, temples and tides.

This isn’t luxury travel, and it’s not backpacker survival mode either. It’s something in the middle. I’m navigating ancient temples and quiet coastlines with a $50-ish/day budget, no brand deals, no retreats, just the next step on a personal journey of resetting my mind, body, and bank account after years of hustling for the “American Dream”, mental fatigue and financial hustle.

As a millennial woman who left the U.S. in 2024 to tackle debt and rediscover herself through slow travel, I’m documenting the honest, sometimes awkward, and always evolving process of rebuilding a life abroad. This piece explores how “peace” looks (and costs) very differently depending on where you are, and who you’re trying to become.

My writing is first-person, witty, reflective, and unapologetically honest. I craft stories for readers who are tired of highlight reels and craving stories that live in the gray areas. This story is for anyone who’s ever felt stuck between what they want and what they can afford, who they are and who they’re becoming.
I’d love to discuss the possibility of contributing this piece to
. Please let me know if you’re interested in collaborating and next steps.
Thank you for your time and consideration thus far!

content.text: PRESS RELEASE: Digital Nomad Illustration Exhibition - UK/Japan
NOMAD: Perspectives on Home in a Changing Japan

Artist Molly Maine and Ryo Osera, Executive Officer of the Japan Digital Nomad Association are available for interview - please do let me know if we can work on anything in the lead-up to the exhibition launch.
NOMAD: Perspectives on Home in a Changing Japan
A Solo Illustration Exhibition by Molly Maine

67 York Street Gallery is proud to present "NOMAD: Perspectives on Home in a Changing Japan," a solo exhibition by renowned illustrator Molly Maine. This thought-provoking exhibition explores the concept of "home" within the context of contemporary Japan, juxtaposing the transient lives of digital nomads with the country's deep-rooted traditions.

Recently ranked the world’s fastest-growing remote working hub, Japan has introduced a digital nomad visa to attract remote workers and support local economies amid a declining, ageing population. At the same time, a new generation of Japanese people is moving beyond their hometowns, significant in a society where generational ties to place have long been central. For others, like evacuees from the Noto earthquake, leaving home is not a choice but a necessity.

A digital nomad for the past nine years, Maine brings a personal lens to the exhibition. The series of illustrations was developed following her 2024 artist residency in Kanazawa, during which she visited the earthquake-stricken Noto Peninsula. Her time in Japan, along with interviews conducted during the residency, directly informed the creation of the work, which draws inspiration from the stories she encountered.
67 York Street Gallery, 67A York St, London W1H 1QB
On the exhibition artist Molly Maine has said,

“As someone who’s lived nomadically for almost a decade, the idea of ‘home’ is something I’ve constantly questioned. This exhibition is a way of exploring that question through the lens of contemporary Japan, a place that continues to shape and inspire my artwork.”

Molly Maine is available for interview and comment, along with Ryo Osera, founder of Colive Fukuoka and co-sponsor of the exhibition. Ryo Osera can talk directly to the new digital nomad visa available in Japan, he is currently Executive Officer of the Japan Digital Nomad Association and founder of Colive Fukuoka having previously worked directly for the late Prime Minister of Japan, Shinzo Abe.

The exhibition will feature 10 pieces of artwork available to purchase as signed, limited-edition prints. PRESS RELEASE: Digital Nomad Illustration Exhibition - UK/Japan

Hello,

Please find pasted below the Press Release on the upcoming illustration exhibition NOMAD: Perspectives on Home in a Changing Japan

Artist Molly Maine and Ryo Osera, Executive Officer of the Japan Digital Nomad Association are available for interview - please do let me know if we can work on anything in the lead-up to the exhibition launch.

Molly

MEDIA RELEASE

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

NOMAD: Perspectives on Home in a Changing Japan 

A Solo Illustration Exhibition by Molly Maine

London, United Kingdom – July 4-13, 2025 

67 York Street Gallery is proud to present "NOMAD: Perspectives on Home in a Changing Japan," a solo exhibition by renowned illustrator Molly Maine. This thought-provoking exhibition explores the concept of "home" within the context of contemporary Japan, juxtaposing the transient lives of digital nomads with the country's deep-rooted traditions. 

Recently ranked the world’s fastest-growing remote working hub, Japan has introduced a digital nomad visa to attract remote workers and support local economies amid a declining, ageing population. At the same time, a new generation of Japanese people is moving beyond their hometowns, significant in a society where generational ties to place have long been central. For others, like evacuees from the Noto earthquake, leaving home is not a choice but a necessity.

A digital nomad for the past nine years, Maine brings a personal lens to the exhibition. The series of illustrations was developed following her 2024 artist residency in Kanazawa, during which she visited the earthquake-stricken Noto Peninsula. Her time in Japan, along with interviews conducted during the residency, directly informed the creation of the work, which draws inspiration from the stories she encountered.

Exhibition Highlights:

  • Dates: July 4-13, 2025

  • Location: 67 York Street Gallery, 67A York St, London W1H 1QB

  • Admission: Free

  • Private View: July 3, 6pm – 8:30pm (Invitation-only event, please RSVP to: molly@mollymainecreative.com 

On the exhibition artist Molly Maine has said, “As someone who’s lived nomadically for almost a decade, the idea of ‘home’ is something I’ve constantly questioned. This exhibition is a way of exploring that question through the lens of contemporary Japan, a place that continues to shape and inspire my artwork.”

Molly Maine is available for interview and comment, along with Ryo Osera, founder of Colive Fukuoka and co-sponsor of the exhibition. Ryo Osera can talk directly to the new digital nomad visa available in Japan, he is currently Executive Officer of the Japan Digital Nomad Association and founder of Colive Fukuoka having previously worked directly for the late Prime Minister of Japan, Shinzo Abe. 

Artwork: The exhibition will feature 10 pieces of artwork available to purchase as signed, limited-edition prints. A special collaborative piece with Japanese artist Yu Yamaguchi, an evacuee from the Noto earthquake, will also be showcased. This unique artwork combines Maine's design with Yamaguchi's traditional lacquered tea container with gold leaf engraving.

Charity Partnership: A portion of the proceeds will support recovery efforts in Noto, Japan, through the Ishikawa Prefectural Community Chest (Red Feather, CCCJ). 

Following its London debut, the exhibition will travel to Japan, showing at lyf Tenjin in Fukuoka from 1–31 October 2025 as part of Colive Fukuoka, one of Asia’s leading digital nomad events, before being exhibited in Tokyo in November 2025.

For more information, interviews, or private tours, please contact molly@mollymainecreative.com 

Website: www.mollymaineillustration.com

Instagram: @molly.creative

Photos

Biographies: 

Molly Maine is a British illustrator from London known for her bold, travel-inspired artwork that combines hand-drawn and digital techniques. A graduate of Falmouth University, she also studied at Nagoya University of Art in Japan, an experience that sparked her lasting interest in Japanese art and culture. Since 2016, Molly has lived and worked as a digital nomad, travelling to over 50 countries while building a freelance illustration and design career ‘on the road’. Her work explores themes of cultural exchange and exploration, and her commercial clients include Sky News, Harvey Nichols, and Lenovo. 

Ryo Osera is a leading voice in the future of work and travel in Japan. Born in Nagasaki, he began his career at Dentsu, where he was appointed as a government supervisor of social marketing to Prime Minister Shinzo Abe (2015-2018). Today, he serves as Executive Officer of the Japan Digital Nomad Association, and directs Colive Fukuoka, one of Asia’s largest digital nomad conferences, and a sponsor of this exhibition.

content.text: This is from Mat Zein, founder of Life in Armenia: (I'll try to be there in person)

"The best time to visit Armenia in 2025 is October, as DigiTec (largest tech show in the region) celebrates its 20th anniversary 💙 Remote workers and tech professionals worldwide are welcomed to join a 7-day intensive program by Nomad Armenia Ltd to integrate into Armenia's tech ecosystem.

Test-drive life in Armenia with zero commitment; stay or go, we’ll support you.
For more details, contact us ASAP

items.title: India’s first digital nomad festival

content.text: Will give you the final detailed optional itinerary with 7 day of leisure and 7 day as digital nomad .
India’s first ever digital nomadic festival
Where Global Digital Nomads Meet the Timeless Nomads of Ladakh**
An Immersive Journey into Culture, Connection, Adventure & Innovation*
Arrival in Leh from Delhi. Hotel check-in and full day at leisure for acclimatization.
Morning visits to Hemis Monastery, Thiksey Monastery, and Shey Palace.
Post-lunch exploration of Shanti Stupa and Leh Market (based on individual acclimatization levels).
Group A: Visit to Basgo Palace, Likir, and Alchi Monasteries.
Group B: Visit to Spituk and Phyang Monasteries. Post-lunch, enjoy white-water rafting at Sangam and experience the world’s highest-altitude zipline.
Journey from Leh to Nubra Valley via Khardung La Pass, accompanied by stories from the historic Silk Route.
Afternoon visits to Diskit Monastery, the towering Maitreya Buddha statue, and the sand dunes of Hunder.
Experience rides on double-humped Bactrian camels—ancient companions of the Silk Route.
Visit Yarab Tso (hidden lake) and relax in the Panamic hot springs.
Full-day excursion to Turtuk, the last Indian village near the Indo-Pak border.
Full-day drive from Nubra to Pangong Lake via Shyok Valley.
Continue the journey from Nubra to Pangong Lake (if not done on Day 4).
Night experience: Stargazing and astrophysics exploration at the Hanle Observatory.
Drive from Hanle to Tso Moriri Lake.
Attend the vibrant Nomadic Festival at Korzok village.
Continue experiencing the Nomadic Festival at Korzok.
Stay in unique rural homestays across Ladakh as a digital nomad.
Immerse yourself in the traditional Ladakhi village lifestyle while working remotely.
Wildlife spotting (snow leopards, Himalayan marmots, etc.)
Astrophysics experiences under clear night skies

items.s91a27d62e:
TADAIMA 2025 is a community-based coliving program held in Shimoda, Japan — where digital nomads and global explorers can truly connect with local people.

Participants can join from just one week, making it accessible even for short-term travelers. Whether you stay for 7 days or a full month, the program offers opportunities to build real friendships with locals, join shared meals, and experience Japanese culture in a deeper, more personal way.

The heart of the program is the Main Week (Nov 11–17), featuring the TADAIMA Mirai Kaigi — a 3-day conference with keynotes, workshops, and community discussions bridging global and local perspectives.

More than just a stay, TADAIMA is a chance to feel at home in Japan — and to create lasting connections that go beyond borders.

items.title: Online Taxman and Entity Inc

content.text: We’re a new brand, but we’ve been doing the same work under our parent company, Online Taxman. Last year, we launched Entity Inc., which focuses primarily on helping non-US individuals set up US companies, although we also work with US expats. The company is US owned by Americans, but our team is spread across the globe, from South America and Europe to the US and Asia (Remote)
In short, it’s the same team behind both Online Taxman and Entity Inc., and we bring over 15 years of experience handling US taxes for expats and global entrepreneurs.

We do have a newsletter and a blog, but our social media reach is still in the early stages as we’re just beginning to publish more content. We’re currently writing a guide called “Should I Form a US Company?” — which could be useful to many nomads — and we always consider the tax and compliance side of things to ensure everything is fully legal and optimized for our clients.

When it comes to our goals, it's quite simple; we'd love to expand our reach and make sure more nomads hear about us. I also believe there's some low-hanging fruit in terms of initial collaboration, whether through content on a blog, social media, or something mutually beneficial.

Our audience is made up of entrepreneurs around the world who find value in having a US company, though the reasons vary. For some, it's about credibility, for others it's access to US banking, payment processors, or entering the US market.

That said, through Online Taxman and also Global Expat Advisors, we also help with more advanced setups and planning for those who need it. Our CEO, Vincenzo Villamena, is also frequently featured on podcasts.
So in terms of the logo and promotion, there’s no rush on our side, I’d be happy to send it over. But I also believe we could collaborate meaningfully on multiple levels.

Last year, we launched Entity Inc., which focuses primarily on helping non-US individuals set up US companies, although we also work with US expats. The company is US owned by Americans, but our team is spread across the globe, from South America and Europe to the US and Asia (Remote)In short, it’s the same team behind both Online Taxman and Entity Inc., and we bring over 15 years of experience handling US taxes for expats and global entrepreneurs.We do have a newsletter and a blog, but our social media reach is still in the early stages as we’re just beginning to publish more content. We’re currently writing a guide called “Should I Form a US Company?” — which could be useful to many nomads — and we always consider the tax and compliance side of things to ensure everything is fully legal and optimized for our clients.When it comes to our goals, it's quite simple; we'd love to expand our reach and make sure more nomads hear about us. I also believe there's some low-hanging fruit in terms of initial collaboration, whether through content on a blog, social media, or something mutually beneficial.Our audience is made up of entrepreneurs around the world who find value in having a US company, though the reasons vary. For some, it's about credibility, for others it's access to US banking, payment processors, or entering the US market.That said, through Online Taxman and also Global Expat Advisors, we also help with more advanced setups and planning for those who need it. Our CEO, Vincenzo Villamena, is also frequently featured on podcasts.So in terms of the logo and promotion, there’s no rush on our side, I’d be happy to send it over. But I also believe we could collaborate meaningfully on multiple levels.

items.title: Workspace 6 (submitted)

content.text: Workspace 6 was founded in 2010 and has been a hub for the creative scene in Amsterdam ever since. Visitors are alway initialy greeted by a mural by local graffiti legends, The London Police and walls, ceilings and aisles of bikes.

Our community spans the gamut from graphic & industrial design to cacoa & kombucha entrepreneurs and, of course, web developers, marketeers, Blockchain, bike PR and even the occasional local cafe owner who we source our coffee beans from.
We have a jazz series with local label Dox Records, screen films, host rides, and serves as a messenger alleycat checkpoint several times a year.
We’re mobbed by BMX’ers every summer for the Bounty Hunters Jam and always have our ramps ready to roll out for impromptu sessions on the bike or skateboard.
One of our confernce rooms is also a music studio with guitar, bass & PA + drums, piano and even a flat screen with an Nintendo 64 and old Xbox!

We love to lunch together either in our dining room, on our patio or around the corner on the water. We’re frequently visited by friends, friends of friends and new firends that are freelancers looking for the coziest, most welcoming spot to hang, work, ride & shred situated under the tracks of Central Station!

items.title: Albufeira Coworking

content.text: It’s really been a ride opening Albufeira coworking!

I, Rebecca, was so fed up by working from the kitchen, longing for connection and community - and together with my partner Ivo, we decided to do something about it. The idea was not only to have a shared space, but create a meeting point and community for people in similar situation. A place to share and exchange ideas, connect and help each other to grow (and have fun of course) . We couldn't be the only ones in Albufeira being in this situation?

After a lot of research and long hunt for the perfect venue (that's a whole another story!) we finally got the keys to Rua do Ténis 13, in the heart of Albufeira 🚪🔑. It’s a small place with 22 seats, but with a lot of heart.
The doors opened at the end of November 2023.

We are so lucky to have a group of amazing people sitting with us 🙌. It's freelancers, entrepreneurs, remote workers and employees, locals and expats, staying long-term and short-term. Programmers, designers, marketers, traders..
Whether you're looking for a place to work, network and grow or simply want to hang out over a beer or two - you are warm welcome to join the community.

items.s5716bab58:
Stayed here for a couple weeks. This place is world class. The apartments are the cleanest I have seen in Central America (and cleaner than any rental I’ve stayed at in the US as well), the internet is fast, the location is fantastic, and the owners are always there to help. This was our first time staying at coconut office, but it surely won’t be our last. I cannot recommend Coconut Office enough.Sebastian Vallone

Morten and Rosalia were the nicest hosts I’ve stayed during my 2 year digital nomad adventure. They make you feel like longtime friends and ensure you have an excellent stay. Morton even drove me to a beach an hour away to surf.
The complex is beautiful. Landscaping is pristine and the pool is both clean and deep. The apartment felt brand new and the kitchen is well stocked.

You can walk to a variety of restaurants and mini markets. They have free bikes you can use for further distances. Uber is also very cheap so a car is not a necessity.

I will definitely be back!Forrest Perry

I had a wonderful stay at the Coconut Office with Morten and Rosalia. Both of them were incredibly kind and welcoming, and they immediately made me feel at home.

During my time there, I had the chance to take an amazing surf lesson with Lucas, go on fantastic nearby trips to Manuel Antonio National Park—where I saw all kinds of wildlife—and visit some of the most beautiful waterfalls I’ve ever seen.
The absolute highlight of my stay was the day in Boca Barranca, which Morten made possible. There, I caught the best wave of my life – an unforgettable experience!
Thank you so much, Morten and Rosalia, for your hospitality and for making my time in Costa Rica truly special. Deniz Ertin

A fantastic place to perfectly combine work and leisure. Rosalia and Morten take great care of their guests. The apartments and workspaces are very comfortable and spacious. Thanks to the proximity to the beach, you can interrupt your workday at any time for a surf trip.
items.title: Coconut Office

content.text: I first visited Costa Rica over 20 years ago. Our car broke down right at the bus stop in Calle Hermosa. I don't know if it was fate, but I rarely have car breakdowns, and perhaps I should have accepted destiny and simply stayed there.
Instead, I only returned many years later and started the Coconut Office.

Playa Hermosa has earned a reputation as one of the world's premier surfing destinations. In 2021, the American non-profit organization, Save the Waves Coalition, selected Playa Hermosa as the 11th World Surf Reserve globally.
The Coconut Office is designed specifically for clients seeking a productive work environment while enjoying surfing and tranquility.

We love spending time with our guests while grilling, surfing, or going on other excursions. Many of the activities we enjoy with our guests are things we ourselves love doing: beach bonfires, cooling down in the river at Playa Hermosa, visiting a nearby waterfall, yoga, skateboarding...

items.title: Vertical Coworking Dom Henrique

content.text: With a modern and sophisticated infrastructure, Vertical Dom Henrique is designed to offer a premium coworking experience, adapted to the needs of professionals, startups, and innovative companies.

Located in one of the city's most emblematic buildings, Vertical Dom Henrique stands out for its contemporary design, large spaces, and impressive views over Porto. The space combines elegance and functionality, providing an inspiring environment for those seeking productivity and well-being in the workplace.
The new space is Vertical Coworking's third unit in the city of Porto, along with Vertical Bolhão and Vertical Firmeza.
As part of Feel Group, Vertical aims to provide unique experiences in its various operations, combining mobility, quality stays, and unforgettable activities.

This coworking space has 40 seats in open space, 156 seats spread over 14 private offices, 5 meeting rooms with capacity for up to 20 people, and a room dedicated to podcasts and streaming. In total, Vertical Dom Henrique has 1600 square metres of pure Flexible Office, ready to provide tailored solutions for any team.

Members have access to premium services, including personalized reception, high-speed internet, relaxation areas, and a workcafe with daily menus suited to the community's tastes. In addition, there is a wellness space that offers classes and events every week, promoting a balance between work and well-being.

The 4th floor also has a rooftop which is freely accessible to the entire community when there are no events taking place. In addition, this floor is prepared for conferences of up to 100 people and events for more than 100 participants.

The space was designed in collaboration with leading companies Feel Arch, responsible for the Architecture and Decoration Project, Alphalink, responsible for project management and supervision, and Sutega, in charge of carrying out the work and coordinating the various subcontracts.

Vertical Coworking reinforces its commitment to flexibility by offering plans that can be adapted to different professional profiles, from freelancers to large companies. It also promotes a dynamic and vibrant community, with exclusive events, workshops, and networking opportunities that foster innovation and professional growth.

items.title: Cowork Funchal

content.text: We have always been passionate about buildings with history. With character.

Twelve years ago, Cowork Funchal was a risky dream of a young entrepreneur in Madeira, when people barely knew what a coworking space was. Today, we are proud of the family we have built, of the many friends who return often because they feel at home here.
We have 5 coworking rooms with 53 desks available; an outdoor patio that charms with its uncompromising charisma, and 24 possible workspaces.
Yes, we've also surrendered to the benefits of having phone booths at the house.
At our place, you'll find 2 meeting rooms and another 2 reserved for training. We are also fortunate to have 11 private offices.

And we could go on, but we prefer to sum it up: at Cowork Funchal, we have plenty of space and are eager to welcome all those who, whether near or far, prefer to work in a suitable space, with the plus of a friendly community.

items.title: The Louise by Clockwise

content.text: Clockwise started with a simple vision: to transform traditional offices into spaces that feel flexible, inspiring, and community-driven. The idea came from noticing how rigid work environments often stifle creativity and connection. We wanted to create places where people genuinely enjoy working and collaborating.

Behind Clockwise is a passionate team dedicated to redefining the workplace experience. From our designers to our community managers, everyone shares the same goal, making work feel effortless and connected.
What makes this location special to you?

Initially, all Clockwise locations were in the UK, but as the concept grew, we expanded across Europe. The Louise location is our second in Brussels, and that makes it particularly exciting. It’s right in the heart of the city’s vibrant business district, yet it feels warm and personal. For me, it’s special because it represents growth and the chance to build a thriving community in a space that truly reflects Clockwise’s values.

items.title: Deutsches Komitee der AIESEC e.V.

content.text: I hope you’ve had a great start to the new year and were able to enjoy the holidays!
I’m finally getting back to you now in the new year regarding our conversation and your really great ideas on how we could work together.

I’ve just added AIESEC to your Nomad Directory (and I hope the information fits well and is easy to understand). We would, of course, be very happy about any posts. Please also let me know if you need anything from us for that.
Thank you very much for sending the magazine. I’m excited to see it! Our headquarters address in Bonn is as follows:

The free issue for our members is definitely a very exciting offer as well! What would the process be here? We’d be happy to share all the details with our members across our various channels. For this, it would be great if you could send us your logo for use, so we can create appropriate posts.

You’re very welcome to feature us on your website, of course – and we can absolutely do the same for AIESEC in Germany. Unfortunately, I don’t have access to other country websites and therefore can’t make this possible there. However, I’d be happy to connect you with other countries that could also be interesting markets for you!
I really like the blog/article idea! Possible topics that come to mind right away (please let me know if and how interesting these are for your target audience):
International professionals in companies (e.g., why this is more than just a “diversity program,” etc.)
What Gen Z expects from the job market and what they are looking for
The impact of volunteering on young students, or the broader topic of volunteering/voluntary work
Leadership (perhaps something along the lines of: “Why leadership development doesn’t only start after graduation”)
Would any of these be interesting? Otherwise, I’m also very open to your ideas and suggestions!

You’re also very welcome to reach out to us regarding your internship positions – for us, it would be especially exciting if you could help shape and experience AIESEC’s vision firsthand! Feel free to send me more details once there’s more clarity within your team.
Let’s also find a time in January to meet and discuss any open points. How does January 16th look for you?
I’m very much looking forward to hearing from you and wish you a wonderful start to the new year!

description.html:
🌿 About Us

Dolce Vita Coliving is a diffused coliving in central Italy for remote workers, digital nomads, and people ready to slow down and reset. It’s a place where focused work blends with authentic human connection and the rhythm of Italian village life.

We are located in Vallo di Nera, one of the most captivating medieval villages in Umbria, less than two hours from Rome and Florence. With just 355 inhabitants, the village offers a peaceful, welcoming atmosphere overlooking the Valnerina valley, surrounded by rivers, forests, and mountains.

Vallo di Nera is proudly recognized as:

  • One of Italy’s Most Beautiful Villages (Borghi più Belli d’Italia)

  • Orange Flag recipient for sustainable tourism

  • Bee-Friendly Municipality

  • Truffle City

Our mission is simple: to foster connection, welcome curious travelers, and create spaces where people can live, work, and recharge at their own pace.

Dolce Vita Coliving follows a diffused coliving model: private rooms, coworking spaces, and shared areas are spread across restored medieval homes, all within a 3-minute walk. Instead of a single building, the village itself becomes your living space—authentic, human, and deeply connected to local life.

Here, you live like a local with modern comforts: fast fiber internet (up to 10 Gbps), well-designed workspaces, and welcoming shared areas. We are an inclusive, sustainable, and pet-friendly community, where connections grow naturally through shared meals, outdoor experiences, and everyday village moments.

Dolce Vita Coliving is not just a place to stay—it’s a slower, more intentional way to live and work in Italy.

items.description_markdown: 🌿 About Us Dolce Vita Coliving is a diffused coliving in central Italy for remote workers, digital nomads, and people ready to slow down and reset. It’s a place where focused work blends with authentic human connection and the rhythm of Italian village life. We are located in Vallo di Nera, one of the most captivating medieval villages in Umbria, less than two hours from Rome and Florence. With just 355 inhabitants, the village offers a peaceful, welcoming atmosphere overlooking the Valnerina valley, surrounded by rivers, forests, and mountains. Vallo di Nera is proudly recognized as: - One of Italy’s Most Beautiful Villages (Borghi più Belli d’Italia) - Orange Flag recipient for sustainable tourism - Bee-Friendly Municipality - Truffle City Our mission is simple: to foster connection, welcome curious travelers, and create spaces where people can live, work, and recharge at their own pace. Dolce Vita Coliving follows a diffused coliving model: private rooms, coworking spaces, and shared areas are spread across restored medieval homes, all within a 3-minute walk. Instead of a single building, the village itself becomes your living space—authentic, human, and deeply connected to local life. Here, you live like a local with modern comforts: fast fiber internet (up to 10 Gbps), well-designed workspaces, and welcoming shared areas. We are an inclusive, sustainable, and pet-friendly community, where connections grow naturally through shared meals, outdoor experiences, and everyday village moments. Dolce Vita Coliving is not just a place to stay—it’s a slower, more intentional way to live and work in Italy.

items.title: Nesting Away

content.text: When Ukrainian-Italian couple Oleksandra and Federico first saw the property three years ago, it was half-abandoned, grey, with an overgrown garden. But they had a vision: a coworking space with panoramic views here, a swimming pool there.

As digital nomads themselves, they knew what remote workers truly needed: not just WiFi and a desk, but a real home and community. After 12 months of renovation, Federico proposed to Oleksandra on the balcony they'd built together.
Fun fact: the family who built the house shares Federico's exact surname, and it sits just 500 meters from the very first property they viewed on their hunt. It felt like destiny.

Today, Nesting Away is central Italy's only coliving designed by digital nomads for digital nomads. Located next to the medieval town of Orte with direct trains to Rome, it's home to remote workers staying 2 weeks to several months - living the vision Ola and Fede saw in that abandoned house years ago.

content.text: Our journey began in 2023 with a simple vision: to create a space where no one has to work alone. We started as a small, tight-knit group of 25 members in a former factory Elma, a place once famous for manufacturing home apliances. We’ve kept that industrious spirit alive (quite literally!). If you walk through our halls today, you’ll find a collection of original Elma irons on display, a nod to the craftsmanship that happened in these very rooms decades ago.

Since those early days, we haven't stopped growing. By expanding our space year after year, we have evolved into a thriving ecosystem. In just two months, we will be celebrating our 3rd anniversary with nearly 110 members. While our square footage has changed, our "Community First" heart remains the same. We aren't just a place to plug in a laptop; we are a strong, connected family that proves we are always better together.

items.title: Altspace Coworking

content.text: Altspace started because Becky (the founder) was watching too many talented, interesting people sit alone in their apartments.

When she moved to Bansko in 2020, there was already this quiet wave of remote workers discovering the town. People came for the mountains, the low cost of living, the skiing…but during the day they were isolated. Working from kitchen tables, fighting with dodgy WiFi and talking to no one. Something about that felt really wrong.
Bansko had all the ingredients for an incredible remote work destination, but it didn’t yet have a space that felt intentionally built for both focus and belonging. So she built one!

Altspace opened in the middle of a global pandemic, which in hindsight sounds mildly unhinged…but the need was obvious. Within a year Altspace had expanded to a second location. By year three, a third. Not because there was some aggressive growth plan, but because the community kept outgrowing the rooms.

From day one, it was never about desks. It was about walking into a room and not having to explain yourself. It was about being surrounded by other people building things, working hard, figuring life out. It was about having deep focus during the day and someone to grab dinner with at night.

Over the years thousands of nomads have come through the doors. Some stay a week, some stay a season, quite a few changed their lives here! Friendships form, businesses launch, relationships start, collaborations happen over coffee that turn into actual companies.
There has also been something unexpected: people choosing to relocate to Bansko permanently because of the community they found inside the Altspace walls.

Altspace has quietly become one of the social anchors of the town. You can ski or hike in the morning, work properly during the day, and find real connection in the evening…not forced networking, just humans being humans.
At its core, Altspace exists to solve a simple problem: remote work doesn’t have to mean remote life.
And in a small mountain town in Bulgaria, that idea has grown into something much bigger than had ever been planned.

content.text: We opened our doors in August 2017 in the heart of the beautiful city of Valletta we call home

Since then we have had the pleasure of welcoming people from different countries, backgrounds and industries. We are pleased to say our lives have been enriched through the community we have built, and hope after some time with us you can say the same.

Both of our sites are a stone’s throw from Saint George’s Square at the very centre of Valletta. One is on the quiet mainly residential Archbishop Street and is a typical Maltese townhouse, full of character and featuring a central courtyard providing plenty of natural light and a rooftop terrace with stunning views across the Grand Harbour towards the 3 Cities. The other site is on top of the Marks and Spencer Building on buzzing Strait Street. It’s an open plan double height 220m2 super modern space with plenty of bare timber and exposed metal framework. Its terrace overlooks Marsamxett Harbour with views towards Sliema

The day to day running of the office is generally in the hands of Iain and Sarah. Ollie and Millie the dogs also chip in by giving everyone a warm and enthusiastic welcome. They’d love to meet your dogs so bring them in!

items.title: Impact Hub Athens

content.text: Impact Hub Athens was founded in 2013, at a time when the concept of social entrepreneurship in Greece was not yet fully developed. There was no clear ecosystem, nor a shared language around impact—but there was a clear need.

We started in a distinctive space in Psyrri with a simple idea: to create a meeting point for people who wanted to work differently more collaboratively, more openly, with a strong orientation toward society and the environment.

At the beginning, we were primarily a community. People with ideas, teams looking for support, professionals who wanted to belong somewhere where entrepreneurship was not measured solely by financial indicators.

Over the years, our role evolved. From a coworking space, we also became an organization designing and implementing programs. We supported early-stage teams as well as mature businesses and organizations seeking to redefine their footprint. We collaborated with public authorities, European institutions, and private partners on projects that went beyond theory and led to tangible outcomes.

Today, Impact Hub Athens is simultaneously a space, a community, and a project implementation organization. It is people working together, programs running in different cities, and partnerships that extend beyond the boundaries of Athens and even beyond Greece.

Over the years, our role evolved. From a coworking space, we also became an organization designing and implementing programs. We supported early-stage teams as well as mature businesses and organizations seeking to redefine their footprint. We collaborated with public authorities, European institutions, and private partners on projects that went beyond theory and led to tangible outcomes.

Today, Impact Hub Athens is simultaneously a space, a community, and a project implementation organization. It is people working together, programs running in different cities, and partnerships that extend beyond the boundaries of Athens and even beyond Greece.

items.title: Stone Soup

content.text: Stone Soup began in 2014, during the economic crisis in Greece, as a Social Cooperative with a clear mission: to support young professionals, unemployed individuals, and students by providing workspace, training, and job opportunities.

We built Stone Soup ourselves. We painted the walls, repaired the infrastructure, and built or sourced the furniture, moving everything into place by hand. The space grew organically through use, shaped by the real needs of the people who worked in it.

From the beginning, we focused not only on infrastructure, but on how a space makes people feel about their work and purpose. Over time, the space evolved into a full coworking hub with private offices, shared work areas, and meeting rooms that adapt to freelancers, startups, and growing teams. What remains unchanged is our commitment to community and collaboration.

We intentionally operate at a human scale. While smaller than large corporate chains, we prioritize quality, reliable technology, and personal support. Our core offering covers essential professional needs, with the flexibility to tailor additional services when needed.

items.title: Culture Co-Working

content.text: Culture Co-Working was created with a simple idea: work should be flexible, inspiring, and connected. As the way people work began to change, we saw a growing need for professional spaces where entrepreneurs, freelancers, remote workers, and companies could work productively without the isolation of working from home.

What started as a vision to create a welcoming and professional workspace quickly grew into a thriving community. By offering modern coworking spaces, private offices, and fully equipped meeting rooms, Culture Co-Working became a place where people not only work—but also collaborate, share ideas, and support one another.

Located in the heart of Cork, our spaces were designed to combine productivity with community. Members benefit from flexible membership options, high-quality facilities, and a network of like-minded professionals who believe that great things happen when people work together.

Today, Culture Co-Working continues to grow as a hub for innovation, collaboration, and business development in Cork. Our mission remains the same: to provide inspiring workspaces where individuals and companies can focus, connect, and build their future.

items.title: The Tara Building

content.text: What began in 2017 with a group of friends and 30 original members has grown into a vibrant community of hundreds. From the very start, Tara was never just about being a workspace – it was sea swims, workshops, rooftop beers, and the buzz of people connecting. Once a vacant site, the building itself has taken many forms over the years, from coworking floors and studios to offices and event spaces – always evolving with the people inside.

From full-time members to day pass visitors, everyone who’s come through our doors has made Tara what it is today. With gigs, talks, pastry mornings and even the odd wedding, The Tara Building has become a community where connections and friendship last well beyond the walls of the building.

items.title: Puzl CowOrKing

content.text: We started as an IT startup. We needed an office. We didn't find one. Long story short, now we make coworking spaces for amazing IT humans. Cool, huh? We design 300 kg desks and get to see how teams build their businesses on them. Oh!, we also get to explore abandoned buildings, walk around barefoot and connect with remarkable people.
To help IT humans and teams grow in a productive environment.

We created Puzl CowOrKing to help IT humans and teams make better products and services. How? By giving them a gorgeous place to work from and a supportive community of like-minded people to share the journey with.

As a company, we measure our success by how well we achieve that mission. It is the achievements of our members and the impact that the environment has on their growth that defines the added value of our business model – not financial ratios.

This is also reflected in the way our Puzl CowOrKing spaces are made. They are not built like common offices. Instead, we design them as community environments which foster efficiency, collaboration, and creativity, both within companies and individuals.

items.title: Madeira Remote

content.text: Casa do Pico is a coliving home created by Madeira Remote, a branch of Madeira Friends, with the mission of connecting locals and internationals and making everyone feel at home on Madeira Island. We created this space for digital nomads looking for the right balance between productivity, rest, community, and island exploration.

Located in central Funchal, Casa do Pico is a spacious T5 house designed for both comfortable living and remote work. The house includes 2 kitchens, 2 living rooms, an office/reading area, a dining area, a backyard with outdoor seating and a jacuzzi, plus a rooftop with beautiful ocean and city views. Each guest also has access to a dedicated desk with a monitor to support a productive work routine.

What makes the experience special is the community around it. Guests get access to Madeira Friends Hub, our coworking space, a discount card with 60+ local partners, networking events, workshops, and two WhatsApp groups: one for the house community and another for the wider digital nomad community on the island. Casa do Pico is more than a place to stay — it is a place to connect, work well, and experience Madeira with like-minded people.

Casa do Pico is a coliving home created by Madeira Remote, a branch of Madeira Friends, with the mission of connecting locals and internationals and making everyone feel at home on Madeira Island. We created this space for digital nomads looking for the right balance between productivity, rest, community, and island exploration.

Located in central Funchal, Casa do Pico is a spacious T5 house designed for both comfortable living and remote work. The house includes 2 kitchens, 2 living rooms, an office/reading area, a dining area, a backyard with outdoor seating and a jacuzzi, plus a rooftop with beautiful ocean and city views. Each guest also has access to a dedicated desk with a monitor to support a productive work routine.

What makes the experience special is the community around it. Guests get access to Madeira Friends Hub, our coworking space, a discount card with 60+ local partners, networking events, workshops, and two WhatsApp groups: one for the house community and another for the wider digital nomad community on the island. Casa do Pico is more than a place to stay — it is a place to connect, work well, and experience Madeira with like-minded people.
